bio: Sit Still is a Bowmanville, Ontario indie rock band whose music draws on post-punk and 2000s alternative rock. The group has released independent projects including Crooked and Finally while remaining rooted in Durham Region's music community. Northern Dial carries Sit Still as part of its Ontario independent rock catalogue.
Toronto-born, Brampton-raised rapper and producer Skip Waiters is a Canadian hip-hop artist whose self-produced work blends poetry, soul, alternative rap and eclectic contemporary production.

Bedford, Nova Scotia-born DJ and producer Skratch Bastid is a leading Canadian turntablist known for technically inventive sets, production work and a career bridging Halifax and Toronto hip-hop communities.
Montréal group Sky was a Canadian R&B-influenced pop-rock act whose self-produced debut Piece of Paradise produced major national radio hits and a Juno Award for New Group of the Year.

Toronto's Skydiggers grew out of the city's late-1980s Queen Street club scene, building a roots-rock sound around Andy Maize and Josh Finlayson's harmonies and songwriting. Their self-titled 1990 debut introduced the band nationally with songs including "Monday Morning" and "I Will Give You Everything," while 1992's Restless became their commercial high-water mark and produced "A Penny More." The momentum carried into Just Over This Mountain and a JUNO Award for Most Promising Group, establishing Skydiggers as a durable Canadian alternative to the louder guitar trends of the period.

Across records including Desmond's Hip City, the band widened its folk, country and rock vocabulary without losing the melodic directness that made its early work distinctive. Skydiggers became less a single-hit story than a long-running part of Canada's roots-rock infrastructure, with extensive touring, changing lineups and a catalogue that connected the Toronto club scene to later generations of independent roots and Americana-adjacent artists.

That longevity is central to why Skydiggers matter. Later releases such as Northern Shore, No. 1 Northern and Warmth of the Sun kept the band active decades after its debut, while No. 1 Northern explicitly revisited Canadian songwriting through material associated with Neil Young, Gordon Lightfoot, Ron Sexsmith and others. Rather than surviving on one nostalgia cycle, Skydiggers built a career around songs, community and a recognizably Canadian roots-rock identity that has remained viable for more than three decades.
Bolton, Ontario singer-songwriter Skye Sweetnam emerged as a Canadian pop-rock artist in the 2000s before evolving into the alternative-metal frontwoman Sever with Sumo Cyco.
Squamish-born DJ and producer Sleepy Tom, born Cam Tatham, is a Canadian electronic artist known for energetic house production and the platinum-certified Diplo collaboration Be Right There.

Sloan formed in Halifax in 1991 around Chris Murphy, Patrick Pentland, Jay Ferguson and Andrew Scott, four musicians who would remain together for decades while sharing songwriting and lead-vocal duties. Their 1992 debut Smeared connected Halifax to the international alternative-rock boom, but the band's deeper significance came from helping build a local ecosystem through its own label, Murderecords. Alongside other East Coast acts, Sloan helped make Halifax one of the most closely watched Canadian indie-rock centres of the 1990s.

After briefly appearing to dissolve, Sloan returned with One Chord to Another in 1996. The record won the JUNO for Best Alternative Album and sharpened the band's balance of power pop, classic-rock craft and four-way songwriting. Navy Blues followed with "Money City Maniacs," while Between the Bridges, Pretty Together and later records demonstrated how the same lineup could keep redistributing creative roles without becoming stylistically static. Their catalogue often draws on older pop and rock traditions, but the personality comes from how differently the four members write inside the same band.

Few Canadian groups have matched Sloan's combination of lineup stability, independent infrastructure and long-term productivity. The band helped define both the sound and the business culture of 1990s Canadian indie rock, then outlasted the scene that first made it famous. More than three decades later, Sloan remains a working example of a band sustained by shared authorship rather than a single frontperson, which is a major part of why its catalogue feels broader than most peers from the same era.

Toronto rapper Smiley is an OVO Sound artist known for a distinctive laid-back cadence, gritty street narratives and an unconventional vocal style that helped make him one of the city's most recognizable contemporary rappers.

Toronto-born Darrin O'Brien, better known as Snow, grew up in North York's Allenbury Gardens in a neighbourhood where Jamaican reggae and dancehall were part of the everyday musical environment. That influence became central to his rapid-fire vocal style and led to a connection with New York rapper and producer MC Shan. Snow's 1993 debut, 12 Inches of Snow, turned that hybrid of reggae, dancehall, rap and pop into an unlikely global breakthrough through "Informer," a song based on his own arrest and incarceration. The single spent seven consecutive weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100, reached No. 2 in the United Kingdom and topped charts in several European markets, making Snow one of the first Canadian urban-music artists of the era to achieve truly international pop scale.

Snow spent the rest of the 1990s resisting the idea that his career could be reduced to one crossover hit. The 1995 album Murder Love was recorded largely in Jamaica and moved further toward dancehall, with appearances and production from established Jamaican artists. The remix of "Anything for You" became a major Jamaican hit, while later records such as Mind on the Moon and Two Hands Clapping returned him to Canadian radio through songs including "Everybody Wants to Be Like You" and "Legal." His catalogue never again matched the extraordinary commercial peak of "Informer," but it showed a sustained commitment to reggae rather than a short-lived stylistic detour.

The long afterlife of "Informer" reinforced Snow's place in Canadian music history. Daddy Yankee reworked its melody and cadence for the 2019 hit "Con Calma," bringing Snow onto a new international chart hit more than 25 years after his debut. In 2023, "Informer" was inducted into the Canadian Songwriters Hall of Fame, recognizing a record that helped make reggae-rap visible inside global pop at a moment when Canadian hip-hop and Caribbean-influenced music still had limited access to the country's mainstream industry. Snow's career is complicated, singular and difficult to separate from the multicultural Toronto environment that shaped his sound, but its scale made him an important early example of Canadian urban music travelling far beyond the domestic market.
Portuguese-Canadian singer-songwriter Sofia Camara, raised in Toronto, writes confessional pop and R&B centred on guitar and voice.
Montréal singer-songwriter Sofia Ly is a Canadian pop and R&B artist whose powerful vocals gained early attention through The Voice before she began releasing original music.

Soft Eyez is a producer and recording artist associated with London, Ontario hip-hop collective 4DaTribe. He has released solo instrumental work and built an extensive collaborative catalogue with KOTO?, including Mornington Me and the 4DaTribe Disc projects. DerekFisher, recorded with KOTO? and chai sully, is his Northern Dial library credit.
Kitchener twin duo Softcult is a Canadian alternative-rock project combining grunge, shoegaze, dream pop and riot-grrrl-inspired DIY values with socially conscious songwriting.

Solar-C is a Canadian hip-hop lyricist associated with the Toronto-area Gillbreathing family alongside Elaquent, Es and Mathematik. His catalogue includes the 2018 album Access To All Lanes, the CrossLakes collaboration Sunshowers and later work with Reazhun, Mathematik and Lanai. His appearance with Mathematik and Es on Elaquent's Carnival is the Northern Dial library credit.

Toronto rapper and producer Solitair is a foundational figure in Canadian hip-hop whose work as an MC, songwriter and producer helped shape major records by Kardinal Offishall, Choclair, Jully Black and others.

Sonny Hendrixx is a Toronto hip-hop artist whose catalogue emphasizes lyrical rap, independent releases and collaborations from the city's contemporary scene. Streaming profiles identify him as a Toronto artist, placing his work within the Greater Toronto Area's current rap ecosystem. Northern Dial carries Sonny Hendrixx as part of its Toronto hip-hop catalogue.

Vernon, British Columbia-born rapper and singer SonReal built a Canadian hip-hop career around melodic songwriting, energetic performances and an alternative-rap sound influenced by classic East Coast hip-hop.

Saanich-born Canadian singer-songwriter and producer Sophia Stel makes hazy, experimental alternative pop shaped by club music, ambient textures and diaristic songwriting. Raised in British Columbia and associated with Vancouver’s creative scene, she broke through with the 2024 EP Object Permanence and followed it with How to Win at Solitaire.
Toronto-born singer-songwriter and designer Sophie Powers is a Canadian artist whose genre-blurring music combines hyperpop, pop-punk, electropop and hip-hop.

Sorisa is a Canadian singer and songwriter from Toronto whose music blends electropop, EDM, hyperpop and melodic hip-hop. He broke through with U Look So Good in Fall and was named one of Billboard Canada's rising Canadian acts to watch in 2026. Northern Dial carries Sorisa as part of its contemporary Toronto pop catalogue.
Québec City group Soul Attorneys is a Canadian pop and R&B band whose late-1990s catalogue produced several Canadian top-10 singles and touring work with Céline Dion.

Vancouver trio soulDecision formed in the 1990s around singer-songwriter Trevor Guthrie, David Bowman and Ken Lewko, developing a polished blend of pop, R&B and dance music at the height of the teen-pop boom. The group was often marketed alongside boy bands, but Guthrie's writing and the band's preference for blue-eyed soul and club production gave the project a somewhat different musical centre. Their 2000 debut No One Does It Better was produced with Charles Fisher and opened with "Ooh It's Kinda Crazy," a sleek pop-R&B single that established the group's Canadian audience.

The major breakthrough was "Faded," which reached No. 1 in Canada and crossed to U.S. radio, while No One Does It Better debuted in the Canadian Top 10. Songs such as "Gravity" and the title track extended the album's run, and soulDecision became one of the relatively few Canadian pop groups of the era to achieve meaningful U.S. exposure in a market dominated by much larger American and British teen-pop machines. The band later released Shady Satin Drug before disbanding in the mid-2000s, after which Guthrie continued as a solo singer and songwriter.

soulDecision matters as part of the pre-streaming Canadian pop infrastructure that existed just before a new generation of Canadian artists began breaking globally with far greater frequency. Their success demonstrated that a Vancouver act working in contemporary R&B and dance-pop could compete inside the turn-of-the-millennium mainstream rather than only on domestic radio. "Faded" remains the defining hit, but the group's strongest material also documents a Canadian attempt to bring songwriter-driven R&B sophistication into the boy-band era.

Jeff 'Spade' Duke is a Scarborough-raised Toronto hip-hop emcee, b-boy, graffiti writer and independent label founder best known as one half of the Canadian rap duo Citizen Kane. Northern Dial's Spade entry is tied to 'Space and Time' from Mathematik's Ecology, a recording credited to Mathematik, Spade and Sic Sense and rooted in the same Toronto underground hip-hop circle.
Montréal rapper Spek, born Hussain Yoosuf, is a Canadian hip-hop artist and former member of Dream Warriors whose career later expanded into music publishing and entrepreneurship.

Halifax rapper Spesh K, born Kevin Kinch, is a longtime East Coast Canadian hip-hop artist whose independent catalogue, MuchMusic exposure and work with the group Fax 4 helped build his reputation in Nova Scotia's rap scene.

Scarborough rapper Spidahman, whose name is also styled Spidah Man, is a veteran member of Toronto’s Monolith collective. His recordings span Monolith’s The Long Awaited... and collaborations with fellow members including Dan-e-o, Wio-K and Grimace Love.

Scarborough rapper Spidahman is a veteran member of Toronto’s Monolith collective whose forceful, battle-ready delivery appears across the crew’s late-1990s and 2000s catalogue. His credits include Monolith’s The Long Awaited..., Dan-e-o records such as Raw Is War and The Real Deal, and Wio-K’s posse cut Ten.

Spirit Josh is a Toronto indie-folk and alternative-country band formed in memory of songwriter Matt Jonn Lewis's late brother Josh. Built around Lewis, Sam Szigeti, Alex Nunes and collaborators, the group has developed a self-recorded catalogue that moves between folk, country, slowcore and indie rock, including Paint a Lucky Picture and the 2026 album Road of Life.
Brampton rapper and community leader Spitty is an Indian-Canadian hip-hop artist whose music blends South Asian samples and instrumentation with North American rap influences.

SRE is a Scarborough, Ontario rapper and multidisciplinary artist whose work blends melodic hip-hop, R&B and visual storytelling. Born and raised in Scarborough, SRE has developed an independent catalogue rooted in the Greater Toronto Area. Northern Dial carries SRE as part of its contemporary Toronto hip-hop catalogue.

Québec City rapper St-Prince, born Brandon Truong, is part of the new generation of francophone urban artists blending melodic trap, contemporary R&B and pop. After emerging with the Sosluv collective, he moved into solo work, signed with Disques 7ième Ciel and released the 2026 EP rien de saint, alongside collaborations with Koriass, FouKi, High Klassified and others.

Maple Ridge, British Columbia rock band Stabilo built a Canadian acoustic-rock and alternative catalogue around dual vocalists, melodic songwriting and radio hits including Everybody and Flawed Design.

Starpainter is a Lethbridge, Alberta band led by songwriter Joel Stretch, with a sound that keeps one foot in indie rock and the other in country. The group's 2026 album Cayenne Flowerbed was produced in Calgary with Chris Dadge and grew into one of Starpainter's most collaborative records. Bright acoustic guitars, slide guitar and loose, detailed percussion sit under songs about distance, routine, absence and the pull of home. Stretch has described Starpainter as a town band that can drift into country tones whenever it wants, and Cayenne Flowerbed leans into that freedom without sanding off the band's prairie character.

Stars began around Torquil Campbell and Chris Seligman before the group settled into Montréal and became closely associated with the city's early-2000s independent-music rise. With Amy Millan and Evan Cranley joining the core, the band developed an elegant form of indie pop built on alternating male-female vocals, electronic texture, chamber-pop detail and lyrics preoccupied with romance, memory and mortality. Heart established the sound, but 2004's Set Yourself on Fire became the breakthrough.

Set Yourself on Fire turned songs such as “Your Ex-Lover Is Dead” and “Ageless Beauty” into enduring Canadian indie staples and earned a JUNO nomination for Alternative Album of the Year. In Our Bedroom After the War expanded the arrangements and political scope, while later albums kept returning to the tension that defined the band from the beginning: intimate relationship writing delivered with theatrical scale. Their connection to the wider Arts & Crafts and Broken Social Scene orbit also placed Stars inside a broader network rather than an isolated scene success.

Stars helped make emotionally literate, orchestral indie pop one of the recognizable sounds of Canadian music in the 2000s. Their longevity matters because the band did not simply preserve the aesthetic of that era; it kept refining a distinctive shared-vocal approach while maintaining an unusually direct relationship with listeners for whom those songs became part of the emotional vocabulary of Canadian indie rock.

Vancouver rock band State of Shock broke nationally with melodic alternative-rock and pop-rock records including Money Honey, building a Canadian catalogue around big hooks and radio-ready guitar music.

Stephen Hero is an East Coast Canadian rapper, songwriter and producer whose work combines alternative hip-hop with a raw working-class perspective. After beginning to record as a teenager, he developed a self-produced catalogue spanning rap, experimental music and live instrumentation, including releases such as Just Because and Let's Get It.
Edmonton pop-rock band Stereos broke nationally after appearing on MuchMusic's disBAND, pairing big pop hooks with electronic and hip-hop-influenced production.

Stone Pöet is a Canadian hip-hop artist associated with Toronto's late-1990s rap scene. He appeared on Maestro Fresh Wes's 1998 album Built to Last, including the Northern Dial track Clap Ya Handz, Turn It Out, Pt. 2, and was identified by Billboard among the Canadian R&B and hip-hop acts supporting the project.
Toronto singer-songwriter and visual artist STORRY is a multidisciplinary Canadian performer whose independent work combines R&B and soul with conceptual storytelling.

Strik-9 is a Canadian hip-hop artist tied to London's early-2000s underground rap scene. He appears with Ron B and E-Mortal on the 2002 track '519 District', a London, Ontario collaboration documented by Penetraitor Records as Canadian rap and associated with the city's local hip-hop roster.

Montréal pop-punk band SUCKERPUNCH! has built its identity around a deliberately direct, high-energy update of the genre’s early-2000s vocabulary. Rather than treating pop-punk as nostalgia alone, the group pairs big melodic hooks and fast guitar arrangements with modern production and a playful self-description built around keeping the music fun, immediate and communal.

The band’s independent releases developed into a rapidly expanding audience through songs such as "99," "Out of My Mind" and "SURVIVE YOU." In 2025 SUCKERPUNCH! signed with Nettwerk Music Group, giving the Montréal group a larger platform as it moved into its 2026 release cycle. The EP WORST PARTY EVER collected singles including "F.O.M.O.," "STANDING OVATION," "TROUBLE" and "RICH!," with a deluxe edition following in September 2026.

Streaming growth, editorial playlist support and appearances around the renewed pop-punk festival circuit have made SUCKERPUNCH! one of the more visible young Canadian bands working in the style. Their role in Northern Dial is as a snapshot of a genre revival that is no longer simply looking backward: Montréal musicians are using the old pop-punk framework as a contemporary independent scene of their own.
Toronto group Sugar Jones was a Canadian pop and R&B girl group created through the first season of Popstars, scoring national radio hits and a platinum-certified debut album in 2001.

Sugar Prince is a Canadian old-school hip-hop artist associated with Vancouver's early-2000s rap scene. He appears with Jah-Fus on the Rascalz track 'Clash (We Don't Play)' from the Vancouver group's 2002 album 'Reloaded' and is catalogued among Canadian old-school hip-hop artists. Northern Dial carries Sugar Prince as part of its classic Canadian hip-hop catalogue.

Toronto-born Canadian rapper, singer and songwriter Sukha, born Sukhman Sodhi, is part of the new generation of Punjabi hip-hop crossing between Canada and India. After breaking out with Siftaan and Same Thing, he expanded his audience with the UNDISPUTED EP, collaborations with artists including AR Paisley and Tegi Pannu and two Juno nominations in 2025.

Parry Sound singer-songwriter Sully Burrows is a Canadian country artist whose small-town Ontario roots shape his contemporary country sound. He emerged with songs including Youth, Think of Me and Rally Around, later becoming a SiriusXM Top of the Country finalist and a CMAOntario Emerging Artist Award winner.

Sumeet is a Canadian singer-songwriter born and raised in London, Ontario whose mid-2000s music blended hip-hop, R&B, dancehall and South Asian influences. Her independent breakthrough included the Elephant Man-assisted single Agony and the album Deeper, with her work receiving Canadian radio play and collaborations across Toronto's urban music scene.

Sunayna Sharma is a Toronto-based singer and songwriter whose soulful vocals move between South Asian pop, R&B and hip-hop. She entered the wider Canadian music conversation through her collaboration with AR Paisley and producers Jay Trak and PVLN on the 2025 single One Way Flight, which is also her Northern Dial library credit.

Sunclef is Toronto producer and DJ Matt Hedlin, an early-2010s fixture in the city's beat scene whose instrumental music blends hip-hop, funk, jazz, electronic music and future soul. His releases include The Tesseract and Attoseconds, alongside production for Buck 65 and collaborations with a l l i e; his feature with a l l i e on 2nd Son's Cluster Flux is the Northern Dial library credit.

Sunny Diamonds is a Toronto music entrepreneur, executive producer and studio operator whose work is rooted in the city's recording scene. Through Diamond Factory Studios he has worked across production, engineering and artist development, while also releasing music under his own name. His 2025 single Caribana Friday is his Northern Dial library credit.
